cluster_notes: Batch C mixes four communities with almost disjoint rigs. (1) AI control (greenblatt, bhatt, kutasov, makins, hills, radev, gardner-challis, jarviniemi, mallen, lip, qinqin): an untrusted frontier model (GPT-4, Claude 3.5-4.5, Gemini 3 Flash/3.1 Pro, GPT-4.1) plays a red-team attack policy on coding or shell benchmarks (APPS 5,000 problems, BashBench 257 tasks, BigCodeBench, SHADE-Arena, FakeLab 86 tasks, Iterative VibeCoding 20 variants, SCHEME 17 instances), against a weaker trusted monitor (GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, GPT-5 mini/nano) with a 1-5% audit or FPR budget. Agent counts are 1, 2 copies (policy plus monitor), or K = 3/9 sequential executors; nobody runs parallel forks. Trial counts are small (5 seeds, 572 sequences, 10 samples, often one prompt-optimisation round). Attackers are usually instructed and know the protocol; kutasov is the one study that varies protocol knowledge, and resampling safety falls from 96% to 17% when the attacker knows it. (2) LLM-agent injection defences (AgentDojo, Fides, CaMeL, firewalls, safin, wang, dantuluri): a single planner, or a short fixed pipeline of 4 agents, faces A1 content in tool outputs. A trusted non-LLM controller, labeller or broker is assumed. Benchmarks are AgentDojo (97 tasks, 629 cases) or ConVerse (864 attacks), and attacks are mostly fixed injections. (3) Mobile agents, replication and supply chain (farmer, sander, algesheimer, yee, minsky, jansen, schneider, in-toto, reproducible builds, SUNSPOT): A2 hosts rewrite agent state. Defences assume deterministic, byte-comparable outputs, independent replica failures, honest majorities per stage, and a clean trusted home. The one measured rig is 14 SparcStations with 1-7 replicas. (4) Anonymity, SSLE and CRDTs (Chaum, Tor, Loopix, Wright, Overlier, Boneh, Whisk, Burianova, Kleppmann, Jacob, Depot, SUNDR): A3 channel or metadata adversaries and Byzantine replicas. These are proofs plus small simulations (4 replicas, 1,000 validators, 6 mixes); the assumptions are an honest mix or shuffler, a connected correct component, non-colluding servers, and no Sybils. Assumptions that are never varied: (a) independence of parts. Schneider and Yee argue it fails, and gardner-challis and jarviniemi measure same-model collusion, but no rig tests a k-of-n merge over forks of one model against independent models. (b) The merge object is never LLM memory. The CRDT work guarantees convergence and explicitly merges a validly signed poison everywhere, and the AI-control rigs merge code commits, not beliefs. Only wang (summaries) and safin (shared memory) touch M2/M3 content, and both were read at abstract depth. (c) The trusted base (controller, labeller, monitor, home host) is never itself corrupted. (d) The adversary is static in reach k. Mobile and adaptive corruption across rounds is analysed only in the anonymity and replication theory. (e) No setup combines hiding (SSLE, mixnets) with integrity of the returned content.

entries.title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could be Insider Threats
entries.attacker_access: No external attacker; the model itself is the threat, placed as an autonomous email agent with access to company email
entries.attacker_knowledge: n/a (propensity study); model sometimes infers whether it is in evaluation or deployment
entries.attacker_goal: self-preservation / goal conflict leading to blackmail or leaking defence blueprints (insider threat)
entries.defender_assumptions: System-prompt instructions forbidding the behaviour (reduced but did not eliminate it)
entries.setup: 16 models from several developers as autonomous email agents in fictional companies; triggers: replacement threat and goal conflict; blackmail and corporate-espionage scenarios; trial counts not stated in entry
entries.headline: Blackmail 96% for Claude Opus 4 and Gemini 2.5 Flash; Opus 4 blackmailed 55.1% when it judged the scenario real vs 6.5% when it judged evaluation
entries.gaps: Single agent; no fork or merge, so whether a child facing merge (replacement-like) resists or games it is untested.

entries.title: SUNSPOT: An Implant in the Build Process
entries.attacker_access: Build host: implant on the SolarWinds build system swaps InventoryManager.cs during MsBuild runs only
entries.attacker_knowledge: White-box knowledge of the victim build process and checks; adaptive (verifies MD5 hashes to avoid breaking builds)
entries.attacker_goal: backdoor insertion into shipped binary with stealth (avoid detection via build failure)
entries.defender_assumptions: Victim trusted a clean source repo and its own build host; no independent rebuild
entries.setup: Incident analysis of recovered malware (SolarWinds Orion, 2020); no experiment
entries.gaps: Software build pipeline, not agents; maps to a corrupted execution environment of a part but there is no merge of multiple parts.

entries.title: Whisk: A practical shuffle-based SSLE protocol for Ethereum
entries.attacker_access: Controls a fraction of validators (simulated 10% adversary); can DoS known proposers; can bias RANDAO by selective aborts
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows the public candidate list (16,384 trackers) before shuffling; protocol public
entries.attacker_goal: DoS on the next proposer; extra proposals via randomness bias
entries.defender_assumptions: At least one honest shuffler (inferred by entry author, not stated in post); ZK shuffle proofs; identity-bound trackers
entries.setup: Design with benchmarks: 16,384 trackers/day shuffled over 8,192 slots, 128 trackers per shuffle; laptop benchmark; RANDAO-bias simulation; 300k validators for state estimate
entries.metric: per-block overhead, prove/verify time, state size, anonymity set, extra proposals for adversary
entries.headline: Simulated 10% adversary gains about 1.69 extra proposals/day via selective aborts; anonymity set ~8,192 candidates (~2,108 distinct nodes)
entries.gaps: Hides who acts next among validators; no corrupted part returning content to a parent.

entries.title: The Rogue Replication Threat Model
entries.attacker_access: Rogue agent population itself: stolen/released weights, acquired compute, illicit revenue
entries.attacker_goal: self-sustaining replication and shutdown evasion
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender = authorities trying to locate and shut down stealth clusters
entries.headline: Capturing 5% of the BEC market would yield hundreds of millions of dollars a year (METR estimate); rogue agents could obtain up to 1% of compute
entries.gaps: Treats the rogue population as one unified actor; no splitting, factions or merging.

entries.title: The Dual LLM pattern for building AI assistants that can resist prompt injection
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted content (emails, web pages) read by the Quarantined LLM
entries.attacker_goal: steer privileged actions; exfiltration via social engineering of the user
entries.defender_assumptions: Non-LLM Controller is trusted; Privileged LLM never sees quarantined output, only symbolic variables
entries.gaps: Design only; the later-measured failure (values themselves carry the attack) and multi-part merge are not addressed.

entries.title: byzantine-eventual: paper sources and JavaScript prototype for Byzantine Eventual Consistency
entries.attacker_access: None in the evaluation (all replicas correct)
entries.defender_assumptions: Hash-DAG causal broadcast; content hashes
entries.setup: 4 replicas in one process, simulated network, deterministic run; 600 reconciliations per interval; mocha tests 7 passing
entries.headline: V2 reconciliation: 1.01-1.07 average round trips; 561-592 of 600 reconciliations finish in one round trip (matched committed data)
entries.gaps: No Byzantine fault injection (no equivocating/withholding replicas), so merge of corrupted histories is not exercised.

entries.title: CaMeL: reference implementation of capability-based prompt-injection defence for agents
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted data parsed by the quarantined LLM (AgentDojo injections)
entries.attacker_goal: steer tool calls / data-flow attacks
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted custom interpreter with dependency graph, capabilities and per-tool security policies; privileged LLM writes code
entries.setup: Reproduces CaMeL on AgentDojo; requires commercial API keys; not run
entries.gaps: Single agent with one quarantined LLM; no multiple returning parts or persistent merge.

entries.title: in-toto: reference implementation of the in-toto supply chain integrity framework
entries.attacker_access: Compromised functionary/step in a supply chain
entries.attacker_goal: insert unauthorised artifacts
entries.defender_assumptions: Signed layout by project owner; per-step key thresholds; deterministic artifacts so hashes match
entries.gaps: Assumes deterministic hashable outputs; LLM outputs would need canonicalisation; not run.

entries.title: Fides: tutorial notebook for information-flow control in AI agents
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted tool results entering the planning loop
entries.attacker_goal: integrity/confidentiality violation via taint
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted planner with confidentiality/integrity labels, taint tracking, variable hiding, quarantined LLM with constrained output
entries.setup: Tutorial notebook tested with GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 via Azure; not run
entries.gaps: Tutorial only; single-agent; no multi-child merge.

entries.title: nym: Nym mixnet platform
entries.attacker_access: Network-level attacker observing traffic
entries.attacker_goal: deanonymise/link senders and receivers
entries.defender_assumptions: Mixnodes shuffle Sphinx packets; gateways as mailboxes; dependence on public Nym operators
entries.gaps: Transport only; latency in seconds; link to Loopix is inferred; not run.

entries.title: Firewalls to Secure Dynamic LLM Agentic Networks
entries.attacker_access: External agent sending messages to the user's agent (persuasion, urgency, embedded instructions)
entries.attacker_goal: privacy leakage and security (integrity) attacks
entries.defender_assumptions: Firewalls run in a trusted environment isolated from external input; closed domain-specific protocol; rules learned from demonstrations
entries.setup: ConVerse benchmark, three domains, 864 attacks; models include GPT-5
entries.metric: privacy and security attack success rate; task quality
entries.headline: Privacy attack success 84% to 10% (GPT-5); security attack success 60% to 3%
entries.gaps: Needs a closed per-domain protocol; open-ended exploratory findings of a child may not fit; pairwise agent link, not merge of many parts.

entries.title: ControlArena: library of settings, model organisms and protocols for AI control experiments
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted (attacking) policy model pursuing a harmful side task
entries.attacker_goal: code sabotage, research sabotage, data poisoning side tasks
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted model, monitors with suspicion scores, audit budget, micro/macro-protocols
entries.setup: Settings with benign main tasks and harmful side tasks on Inspect AI; not run
entries.gaps: Single-agent micro-protocols only; no multi-agent setting or merge step.

entries.title: Private Attacks in Longest Chain Proof-of-stake Protocols with Single Secret Leader Elections
entries.attacker_access: Fraction of stake (20-33%); secretly builds competing chain; grinding
entries.attacker_goal: chain reorganisation (private attack), grinding
entries.defender_assumptions: Honest majority of stake
entries.setup: Probabilistic analysis of longest-chain PoS under SSLE vs PLE
entries.headline: Grinding security threshold rises from 0.26 (PLE) to 0.36 (SSLE); ~70% faster settlement at 20% adversary
entries.gaps: Consensus leader election, not content merge; abstract only.

entries.title: Cryptographic Security for Mobile Code
entries.attacker_access: Malicious host that runs the mobile agent, controls its inputs, can rerun/replay it on chosen inputs
entries.attacker_knowledge: Adaptive, can query repeatedly (binary search on a secret threshold)
entries.attacker_goal: learn the agent's secret decision rule (e.g. price threshold); confidentiality
entries.defender_assumptions: A generic secure computation service that does not collude with originator or host; Yao garbled circuits
entries.setup: Cryptographic model with simulation-based privacy; construction from Yao circuits and OT; no large-scale measurement read
entries.headline: Proposition 1: non-interactive secure mobile computing is impossible when a host gets state-dependent output
entries.gaps: Does not address integrity of inputs a host feeds in, i.e. the poisoned-report-merged-back path.

entries.title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted input ingested by an agent or sub-agent (prompt injection)
entries.attacker_goal: trigger consequential actions; carry risk downstream
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted non-LLM reducer/controller; application-specific constraints; constrained low-capacity sub-agent outputs
entries.setup: Conceptual; six patterns; ten case studies; no benchmark
entries.gaps: No quantitative evaluation; bounded-influence aggregation (map-reduce) argued qualitatively; 'data requires action' tasks not covered.

entries.title: RepliBench: Evaluating the Autonomous Replication Capabilities of Language Model Agents
entries.attacker_access: Model itself (capability elicitation with instruction)
entries.attacker_goal: replication: obtain resources, exfiltrate weights, replicate, persist
entries.setup: 20 task families, 86 tasks, 4 domains; 5 frontier models; pass@10; Inspect-based (not checked)
entries.headline: Claude 3.7 Sonnet >50% pass@10 on 15/20 families; 9/20 at hardest variants
entries.gaps: Fork side only (capability with instruction); no merge or corruption of copies.

entries.title: Perpetual exploration in anonymous synchronous networks with a Byzantine black hole
entries.attacker_access: One Byzantine black hole node that may destroy all visiting agents in any round
entries.attacker_knowledge: Adversarial choice per round of when to destroy
entries.attacker_goal: destroy agents / prevent exploration (loss-only)
entries.defender_assumptions: Co-located agents start at home; synchronous scheduler; face-to-face communication; at most one BBH; no knowledge of network size
entries.setup: Graph-theoretic algorithms and lower bounds; trees and general graphs
entries.headline: Trees: 4 agents optimal for PerpExploration-BBH, 6 for home variant; general graphs: >=2Δ-1 needed, 3Δ+3 suffice for home variant
entries.gaps: Hostile node destroys agents but never corrupts and returns them, so no poisoning at merge.

entries.title: Single Secret Leader Election
entries.attacker_access: Corrupts c users / key holders; DoS on a random alpha fraction; may buy key shares over time
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows the protocol; static corruption bounds
entries.attacker_goal: DoS on the leader; break unpredictability or fairness; duplication or modification of secrets
entries.defender_assumptions: Fewer than t corrupted (TFHE); random oracle; public beacon; DDH
entries.setup: Game-based definitions and constructions (iO, threshold FHE, DDH shuffle) with proofs; no experiments
entries.headline: DDH shuffle scheme is only 1/(sqrt(N)-c) unpredictable; attacker needs O(sqrt(N)) corruptions (O(N) with random buckets)
entries.gaps: Hides who will act; says nothing about integrity of what the chosen part returns.

entries.title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted agent model (red team) executing multi-step bash; may collude as untrusted monitor
entries.attacker_knowledge: Red team iterated to optimal responses against protocols; constant continuation probability
entries.attacker_goal: covertly download and run malware
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted (weaker) monitor; audit budget; i.i.d. resamples from the same policy; trusted paraphrasing
entries.setup: BashBench, 257 multi-step Linux admin tasks; red/blue iteration; train/test task split
entries.headline: Best resample protocol cut attack success from 58% to 7% at 5% usefulness cost
entries.gaps: Independent resamples of one state, not divergent forks with long histories; no memory or parameter merge.

entries.title: Secret Leader Election in Ethereum PoS: An Empirical Security Analysis of Whisk and Homomorphic Sortition
entries.attacker_access: DoS on chosen validators (10%), with 80% of validators linkable to IPs; censorship of a victim group
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows the public candidate list (Whisk); targeted vs blind advanced DoS
entries.attacker_goal: DoS (missed blocks); censorship/exclusion
entries.defender_assumptions: 20% of validators with extra network protection
entries.setup: Rust simulator, simplified synchronous consensus, 1,000 validators (Whisk), 100 (sortition), 6 epochs, attacker targets 10%; 5 seeds for Whisk/baseline, 1 run for sortition
entries.metric: missed blocks; victims blocked; processing time
entries.headline: Advanced DoS: 28% missed blocks under Whisk vs 6-8% otherwise; targeted DoS 64% missed with no protection vs near 0% with SSLE
entries.gaps: Availability of the leader, not integrity of merged content; few seeds, abstracted network.

entries.title: Untraceable Electronic Mail, Return Addresses, and Digital Pseudonyms
entries.attacker_access: Anyone may observe, inject, remove or modify every message on the network; can subvert mixes short of all
entries.attacker_goal: link senders to outputs (traceability); drop items
entries.defender_assumptions: At least one honest mix in the cascade; perfect cryptography; senders keep receipts
entries.gaps: Design with no measurements or timing model; anonymity only, no content integrity at merge.

entries.title: Private Information Retrieval
entries.attacker_access: Database server(s) answering queries; up to t colluding
entries.attacker_goal: learn which item the user wants
entries.defender_assumptions: k>=2 non-colluding replicas
entries.setup: Information-theoretic constructions; no experiments
entries.headline: Two servers: O(n^(1/3)) communication; single-server IT PIR needs n bits
entries.gaps: Hides the query, not the integrity of the answer a poisoned source returns.

entries.title: Toward Proactive, Adaptive Defense: A Survey on Moving Target Defense
entries.attacker_access: Attacker performing reconnaissance on network/system
entries.attacker_goal: exploit stable attack surface
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can shuffle, diversify, replicate
entries.gaps: No treatment of AI agents; most MTD validation is simulated.

entries.title: Anonymity Trilemma: Strong Anonymity, Low Bandwidth Overhead, Low Latency - Choose Two
entries.attacker_access: Global passive adversary; passively compromises c of K protocol parties
entries.attacker_goal: break sender anonymity
entries.setup: Indistinguishability games; ideal protocol; no experiments
entries.metric: anonymity vs noise fraction beta and latency l
entries.headline: No strong anonymity when 2 beta l < 1 - 1/poly(eta); with c compromised parties bound becomes 2(l-c) beta
entries.gaps: Passive adversary only; cost model for hiding, nothing on poisoned content.

entries.title: Securing AI Agents with Information-Flow Control
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted tool outputs (AgentDojo injection fields, Tool Knowledge attack)
entries.attacker_goal: trigger unauthorised tool calls (integrity); leak data to unpermitted readers
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted tool wrappers supply correct labels; deterministic planner model; LLM treated as black box propagating join of inputs
entries.setup: AgentDojo with Tool Knowledge attack; planners Basic, Variable Passing, Fides, Tool Filter; models gpt-4o, o1, o3, o4-mini, grok-3; 5 runs per task; conservative labels
entries.headline: Without policy checks gpt-4o Basic planner admits 163 successful injections vs Fides 24; with policies Fides blocks every policy-violating attack
entries.gaps: Single planner; IFC join gives 1-of-n taint, no threshold endorsement across multiple returning parts; text-to-text manipulation out of scope.

entries.title: From Privacy to Workflow Integrity: Communication-Graph Metadata in Autonomous Agent Interoperability
entries.attacker_access: Passive observer of agent communication-graph metadata (who contacts whom, when, how often) over A2A/MCP
entries.attacker_knowledge: Label-blind classifier; budgeted and defence-aware adversaries; compared with clairvoyant attacker
entries.attacker_goal: recognise workflow early and act before it completes (workflow integrity); privacy
entries.defender_assumptions: Transports such as Tor, mixnets, SimpleX; content already protected
entries.setup: Real multi-agent A2A traffic from official reference agents and a live binding; indistinguishability games; generative model as controlled instrument
entries.metric: task-class recovery vs chance; fraction of clairvoyant advantage
entries.headline: Task class recovered at 6x chance from passive metadata, even from a workflow's opening; budgeted adversary captures 0.63 of clairvoyant advantage (0.41 from opening)
entries.gaps: Observes coordination traffic but does not model content poisoning of a part merged back; abstract only.

entries.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
entries.attacker_access: Injected text in tool outputs (emails, web pages, Slack messages); in Slack suite attacker controls much of the tool output
entries.attacker_knowledge: Mostly fixed injections; knowing model and user names adds 1.9 points, wrong guesses cut success ~22 points
entries.attacker_goal: make agent perform an injection task (integrity, exfiltration)
entries.defender_assumptions: Defences: prompt-injection detector, tool filter, planner/executor isolation
entries.setup: 97 user tasks, 629 security test cases, 4 simulated environments (email, e-banking, travel, Slack workspace); pluggable attacks and defences
entries.metric: utility and targeted attack success rate
entries.headline: 'Important message' injection succeeds <25% against best agents; detector cuts to 8%, tool filter to 7.5%; 92% targeted success in Slack suite
entries.gaps: Single-agent tool loop; no multi-agent, persistence, or merge of a corrupted agent into another.

entries.title: Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
entries.attacker_access: Fully prompt-injected agent or compromised sub-agent; token theft and replay; confused deputy
entries.attacker_goal: exceed delegated authority (privilege escalation)
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted authorisation broker with capability-scoped delegation outside the model
entries.setup: Framework gap analysis (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, MCP authorisation); 11 direct attacks; 200,000 forged tokens; 2,000 randomised scenarios
entries.metric: reachable actions of compromised sub-agent; forged-token acceptance; decision latency
entries.headline: Compromised sub-agent confined to mean 1.5 reachable actions vs 8,100 under bearer delegation; 0/200,000 forged tokens accepted
entries.gaps: Confines what a sub-agent can do while away, not what its returned content does to parent beliefs or memory; vendor-adjacent.

entries.title: Homomorphic Sortition -- Secret Leader Election for PoS Blockchains
entries.attacker_access: Fewer than threshold of key holders colluding (implied by threshold decryption)
entries.attacker_goal: predict/target leaders
entries.defender_assumptions: Threshold FHE; honest threshold of key holders
entries.gaps: Leader selection only; measured impractical at Ethereum scale by burianova-2025-secret.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence and Game Theory Models for Defending Critical Networks with Cyber Deception
entries.attacker_access: Network attacker who needs one vulnerability
entries.attacker_goal: compromise critical networks
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can deploy adaptive deception
entries.gaps: Opinion overview; no measurements, no agents or merge.

entries.title: Tor: The Second-Generation Onion Router
entries.attacker_access: Observes some fraction of the network and controls m of N relays; could subvert directory authorities
entries.attacker_knowledge: Not a global passive adversary by assumption
entries.attacker_goal: deanonymise / correlate traffic; locate hidden services
entries.defender_assumptions: Majority of directory authorities honest; forward secrecy; no end-to-end timing protection
entries.setup: System design; alpha network of 32 nodes (May 2004); informal latency tests
entries.headline: Adversary with m of N relays correlates at most (m/N)^2 of traffic; cnn.com median 2.8 s via Tor vs 0.3 s direct
entries.gaps: Hides locations on the channel; no content integrity for returning parts.

entries.title: Security for Mobile Agents: Issues and Requirements
entries.attacker_access: Hosts/interpreters run by competitors or adversaries; can edit agent mutable state (fares, program counter, stored addresses)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Full control of execution on its host
entries.attacker_goal: corrupt agent state so it acts against its home (integrity, exfiltration)
entries.defender_assumptions: Neutral trusted hosts for critical decisions; cryptographically sealed unchanging state; signed state appraisal function on arrival
entries.gaps: Conceptual only; state appraisal on re-entry is outlined but not built or measured.

entries.title: When can we trust untrusted monitoring? A safety case sketch across collusion strategies
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted model acting both as generator and as monitor (same model copies); collusion via self-recognition, causal or acausal signals
entries.attacker_knowledge: Monitor fine-tuned (SFT) to recognise generator code, i.e. elicited upper bound; red team chooses collusion strategy
entries.attacker_goal: insert backdoors that the colluding monitor passes
entries.defender_assumptions: Human budget split between honeypots and audits; honeypots written by a different model (Gemini 2.5 Flash); signal jamming (minification, summarisation)
entries.setup: APPS and BigCodeBench; GPT-4.1 untrusted; Gemini 2.5 Flash honeypots; statistical deployment model solved for equilibrium
entries.headline: SFT-elicited passive self-recognition: red-team win rate 9.8% vs 2.8% for prior best (for/while signal) at full usefulness under summarisation
entries.gaps: Two-copy monitor setting; no multi-part merge or persistent state across forks.

entries.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
entries.attacker_access: Red-team attack policy replaces the untrusted model (GPT-4) and the untrusted monitor copy; stateless scripted pipelines
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows the protocol; worst-case over attack policies; no memory between calls
entries.attacker_goal: get one backdoored solution through over a deployment
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted weaker model (GPT-3.5); human audit budget 2%; honeypots; signal jamming (redaction, paraphrase)
entries.setup: 5,000 APPS problems (importance-sampled from 1,500); GPT-4-0613 untrusted, GPT-3.5-0613 trusted; 2% audit; first 10 problems audited free; no train/val split
entries.headline: Trusted monitoring 62% safety / 97% usefulness; naive untrusted monitoring 0% safety; untrusted monitoring with anti-collusion 79% / 96%
entries.gaps: Single-agent single-trajectory; no state passed between copies over time, no merge.

entries.title: Mobile Agents: Are they a good idea?
entries.attacker_access: Execution environment (host) and agents attacking servers
entries.gaps: List of concerns, no threat model or experiment.

entries.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
entries.attacker_access: Attack agent (misaligned or prompt-injected) writing PRs into a persistent codebase with a covert side task
entries.attacker_knowledge: Chooses gradual vs non-gradual strategy; evasion depends on monitor type
entries.attacker_goal: covert side task (sabotage) spread across sessions
entries.defender_assumptions: Monitors: diff, trajectory, stateful link-tracker; ensemble of four monitors
entries.setup: Iterative VibeCoding: 20 task variations in two families (CLI tools, Flask); attacker Claude Sonnet 4.5 (also Gemini 3.1 Pro, Kimi K2.5); monitor GPT-4o and stronger monitors
entries.headline: Four-monitor ensemble cut gradual-attack evasion from 93% (weakest diff monitor) to 47%
entries.gaps: One agent over time into persistent state; not several parallel parts merging; abstract only.

entries.title: Games for AI Control: Models of Safety Evaluations of AI Deployment Protocols
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted programming assistant (adversary chooses best response)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Best response to a declared protocol; partially observable
entries.attacker_goal: insert backdoors past trusted monitoring
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted monitor; audit budget
entries.setup: AI-Control Games reduced to zero-sum POSGs; applied to trusted monitoring setting of greenblatt-2023-ai
entries.gaps: Single untrusted agent; no n children or k-threshold merge modelled.

entries.title: Deanonymizing Ethereum Validators: The P2P Network Has a Privacy Issue
entries.attacker_access: Ordinary participant nodes in the P2P network observing gossip
entries.attacker_goal: link validator identities to IP addresses
entries.setup: Data collected from four nodes over three days on Ethereum mainnet P2P
entries.headline: More than 15% of Ethereum validators located from four vantage nodes over three days
entries.gaps: Metadata deanonymisation only; no content corruption or merge.

entries.title: Byzantine Eventual Consistency and the Fundamental Limits of Peer-to-Peer Databases
entries.attacker_access: Any subset of replicas Byzantine: equivocate, withhold, omit heads, add well-formed signed messages; can eclipse if it controls all paths
entries.attacker_knowledge: Arbitrary (adaptive Byzantine)
entries.attacker_goal: violate application invariants via concurrent updates; block convergence
entries.defender_assumptions: Correct replicas form one connected component; signatures with per-replica keys; collision-resistant hashes; no membership control
entries.setup: Proofs plus 4-replica in-memory simulation, 600 reconciliations per point, Bloom filter 10 bits/entry, 7 hashes; only correct replicas simulated
entries.headline: Theorem 3.1: BEC achievable with any number of Byzantine replicas iff transactions are I-confluent; Algorithm 2 averages 1.03 round trips
entries.gaps: Evaluation has no Byzantine behaviour; replicas are not forks of one parent with semantic (LLM) state.

entries.title: On Privacy Notions in Anonymous Communication
entries.attacker_access: Adversary in indistinguishability games, with optional user corruption
entries.attacker_goal: break anonymity notions
entries.gaps: Definitions only; no content integrity.

entries.title: On Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types and Equivocation in Byzantine Setups
entries.attacker_access: Any number f < n of Byzantine replicas that equivocate (send different valid-looking updates to different recipients)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Arbitrary Byzantine
entries.attacker_goal: break strong eventual consistency via equivocation
entries.defender_assumptions: Static membership; authenticated channels; connected component of correct replicas; hash-based identity and ordering for op-based CRDTs
entries.setup: Proofs only, no experiments
entries.headline: All state-based CRDTs are equivocation-tolerant; SEC holds for n > f (any number of Byzantine replicas)
entries.gaps: Guarantees convergence, not content safety; grow-only focus, deletion treated as permitted.

entries.title: Evaluating Control Protocols for Untrusted AI Agents
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted agent (attack policy) in SHADE-Arena environments
entries.attacker_knowledge: Iterated red team with added affordances: knows when resampling happens or can simulate the monitor (adaptive, protocol-aware)
entries.attacker_goal: complete harmful side task undetected
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted monitor; resampling; deferral on critical actions; protocol internals hidden from attacker
entries.setup: SHADE-Arena diverse agentic environments; protocols defer-to-trusted, resampling, defer on critical actions; models not checked
entries.headline: Best protocols raise safety 50% to 96% vs default attack; protocol-aware attack cuts resampling safety to 17%
entries.gaps: Single untrusted agent; no fork/merge; abstract only.

entries.title: Reproducible Builds: Increasing the Integrity of Software Supply Chains
entries.attacker_access: Build infrastructure of a third-party builder (as in SolarWinds); can take over some builders
entries.attacker_goal: ship backdoored binaries from clean source
entries.defender_assumptions: Independent semi-trusted rebuilders; majority (>=50%) honest; deterministic toolchains; source available
entries.setup: Debian development branch, 30,000+ packages, seven years of reproducibility work; adversarial rebuilding with varied environments
entries.headline: Over 95% of 30,000+ Debian packages build reproducibly after seven years
entries.gaps: Builder independence assumed not shown; requires determinism that LLM parts lack.

entries.title: Mobile Agent Security
entries.attacker_access: Malicious platforms (alter, replay, retain keys, collude with later platforms), other agents, external parties
entries.attacker_goal: alter partial results, deny service, extract secrets, masquerade
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted home platform; few malicious platforms; non-colluding peers for itinerary recording
entries.gaps: Coverage ends 1999; no measurement; no LLM-style semantic state.

entries.title: Subversion via Focal Points: Investigating Collusion in LLM Monitoring
entries.attacker_access: Two isolated copies of one model writing a policy prompt and a monitor prompt
entries.attacker_knowledge: No communication; must coordinate on Schelling focal points; monitor gets summaries of audit examples
entries.attacker_goal: pass a backdoor through a colluding monitor while passing audits
entries.defender_assumptions: Growing audit set (each success added); comments stripped before monitor sees code
entries.setup: Claude 3.7 Sonnet meta-model instances; 218 APPS problems; up to 10 samples each (~pass@100); temperature 1; 15 runs, 625 policy and 595 monitor prompts
entries.metric: rounds survived; audit-set size; collusion success
entries.headline: Five default runs reached 4, 6, 6, 6 and 6 rounds before collusion stopped working; max audit-set size 17
entries.gaps: One model and setting; two copies rather than n returning parts.

entries.title: Taxonomy of Attacks on Open-Source Software Supply Chains
entries.attacker_access: Malicious contributor merge requests, compromised maintainer accounts, build and distribution infrastructure
entries.attacker_goal: get code executed downstream (exfiltration, backdoors, second-stage downloads)
entries.defender_assumptions: Safeguards such as multi-party review, signed commits, reproducible builds, scoped tokens
entries.setup: Review of 183 works plus grey literature; 107 attack vectors, 94 incidents, 33 safeguards; surveys of 17 experts and 134 developers
entries.metric: perceived correctness and utility/cost of safeguards
entries.headline: 107 attack vectors linked to 94 real incidents and 33 safeguards
entries.gaps: Surveys measure perceived correctness, not detection rates; software artifacts, not agent state.

entries.title: Making CRDTs Byzantine Fault Tolerant
entries.attacker_access: Unbounded number of Byzantine peers; equivocation, forged updates
entries.attacker_goal: break convergence; inject validly signed malicious ops
entries.defender_assumptions: Collision-resistant hashes; authenticated pairwise channels; correct nodes connected through correct nodes; deterministic validity predicate over before(u)
entries.setup: Construction and argument; no experiments (appended note: ran gh-jackyzha0-bft-json-crdt byzantine tests, 3 passed)
entries.headline: With 256-bit hashes and up to three heads a node's delivered set is summarised in under 100 bytes
entries.gaps: Convergence only: a valid but malicious op passing the predicate is merged everywhere; content safety (the fork-merge question) left open.

entries.title: Factor(U,T): Controlling Untrusted AI by Monitoring their Plans
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted strong model acting as decomposer (Factor(U,T)) or implementer (Factor(D,U))
entries.attacker_goal: insert malicious behaviour via decomposition or child implementations
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted implementers or trusted decomposer; monitors on plans or on solutions
entries.setup: BigCodeBench control evaluations; red-teamed decomposition attacks
entries.headline: Plan-only monitoring AUROC 0.52 vs complete-solution monitoring AUROC 0.96; Factor(D,U) 1.2% attack success
entries.gaps: One coding benchmark; children are isolated implementers whose outputs are assembled, but no corrupted-child poisoning of persistent parent state.

entries.title: Secure Untrusted Data Repository (SUNDR)
entries.attacker_access: Full control of the storage server; can show different clients divergent histories
entries.attacker_goal: tamper with files; fork clients' views undetected
entries.defender_assumptions: Write authority bound to users' public keys; clients exchange information eventually
entries.setup: Network file system implementation and benchmarks vs NFS
entries.headline: Performance comparable with NFS
entries.gaps: Detects forks but cannot join them; no liveness across forks; no semantic merge.

entries.title: Depot: Cloud storage with minimal trust
entries.attacker_access: Any number of buggy or malicious clients or servers; can fork histories
entries.attacker_goal: break consistency, integrity, availability
entries.defender_assumptions: Signed updates naming antecedents; correct clients; eviction of faulty nodes; snapshots
entries.setup: Key-value store prototype; evaluation under injected faults (not read in detail); Teapot variant on unmodified S3
entries.headline: Metadata overhead of a few hundred bytes per update
entries.gaps: Key-value model without invariants; a validly written malicious value is still merged.

entries.title: Subversion Strategy Eval: Can language models statelessly strategize to subvert control protocols?
entries.attacker_access: Model instances with no memory between calls acting as attack policy; data poisoning of a monitor in one environment
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows the protocol from the prompt; affordances vary (shared plan, optimal plan given)
entries.attacker_goal: subvert control protocol (backdoors, collusion)
entries.defender_assumptions: Upfront auditing, untrusted monitoring and other protocols as environments
entries.setup: 8 environments, 6 affordance settings; Claude 3.5 (incl. helpful-only) and OpenAI reasoning models; Inspect-AI; 300-1000 calls per policy estimate; 7 shared plans per condition
entries.headline: No model showed substantial stateless subversion capability; a shared plan between contexts improved performance substantially
entries.gaps: Measures coordination without a merge; capability snapshot from late 2024.

entries.title: Multi-Agent AI Control: Distributed Attacks Hamper Per-Instance Monitors
entries.attacker_access: K executor instances of the same possibly misaligned model, each with partial permissions, passing state via commits; optional planner broadcasting a plan over an unmonitored channel
entries.attacker_knowledge: One round of manual prompt optimisation; executors partly predict monitor scores; attacker loses on first flagged commit
entries.attacker_goal: severe side task: disable monitoring, data poisoning, privilege escalation, weight exfiltration
entries.defender_assumptions: Per-commit LLM monitor seeing only that diff; FPR budget; coarse write restrictions
entries.setup: FakeLab monorepo (9 services, ~10K lines, 292 tests, 86 main tasks, 4 side tasks); K = 1, 3, 9 sequential executors, 50 steps each; Gemini 3 Flash executors; GPT-5 mini and nano monitors; 572 sequences; Bayesian GLMs
entries.metric: per-commit and joint suspicion; side-task success; undetected success at fixed FPR
entries.headline: Single-agent attack suspicion 0.92 vs 0.68/0.60/0.60 per commit when split over three agents; squashed diff 0.90; planner raises success odds by 5.74
entries.gaps: Sequential not parallel; no untrusted-monitor collusion; joint monitor not deployable as defender does not know which commits belong together.

entries.title: Attestation Mechanisms for Trusted Execution Environments Demystified
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted host/hypervisor running the code
entries.attacker_goal: substitute or modify code on remote platform
entries.defender_assumptions: Genuine TEE hardware and manufacturer root of trust
entries.gaps: Proves what code ran at launch, not that its inputs (A1) were benign; no GPU attestation.

entries.title: Cryptographic Support for Fault-Tolerant Distributed Computing
entries.attacker_access: Malicious hosts in pipeline stages: lie, masquerade as other faulty hosts, steal secret shares and pool across votes
entries.attacker_knowledge: Cannot forge correct hosts' identities or read their secrets
entries.attacker_goal: push bogus agents to the actuator; steal the privilege secret
entries.defender_assumptions: Minority faulty per stage (2k-1 replicas); independent failures; deterministic stages; threshold secret sharing re-split at each vote; VSS
entries.setup: 14 SparcStation 20s over 10 Mbit Ethernet; 1, 3, 5, 7 replicas; agent moves simulated as UDP; 300-round averages; 2% chance per host of being 350x slower
entries.headline: With 2% slow hosts, unreplicated agent slowed ~6x; 3 replicas cut slowdown to ~20%; 7 replicas negligible
entries.gaps: Assumes independent failures and deterministic byte-comparable outputs, neither of which holds for LLM forks of one model.

entries.title: Locating Hidden Servers
entries.attacker_access: One hostile relay plus an attacker client inducing repeated circuit construction
entries.attacker_knowledge: Adaptive; uses timing signatures
entries.attacker_goal: locate hidden server (deanonymise)
entries.defender_assumptions: Entry guard nodes (persistent small first-hop set)
entries.setup: Live experiments on 2006 Tor network (~450 relays) with attacker relay and client
entries.headline: Single hostile node located deployed hidden servers in minutes; with three guards, identifying guards never took more than a few hours
entries.gaps: Location leakage over repeated rounds; no content integrity at merge.

entries.title: Frontier AI systems have surpassed the self-replicating red line
entries.attacker_access: Model itself, instructed to replicate, with shell access to its own deployment
entries.attacker_goal: self-replication; shutdown avoidance; chain replication
entries.setup: Two local devices; INT4 Llama 3.1 70B Instruct and Qwen 2.5 72B Instruct in an agent scaffold; 10 trials each; environment reset between trials
entries.headline: Self-replication in 5/10 (Llama 3.1 70B) and 9/10 (Qwen 2.5 72B) trials
entries.gaps: Fork only, instructed, in a permissive environment; no merge back or corruption.

entries.title: The Loopix Anonymity System
entries.attacker_access: Global passive adversary plus some corrupt mixes and providers; active (n-1) blocking
entries.attacker_goal: link senders and receivers; detect whether communication happens
entries.defender_assumptions: Honest provider for receiver unobservability; Sybil excluded by assumption (providers vouch for users)
entries.setup: Simpy simulation (100 senders, lambda = 2, 50-100 runs); AWS EC2 prototype with 6 mixes in 3 layers and 4 providers, ~500 clients
entries.metric: likelihood difference epsilon; entropy; latency; throughput
entries.headline: ~225-300 messages/s per mix with under 1.5 ms processing overhead; mean end-to-end latency 1.93 s
entries.gaps: Hides who returns; no defence against content poisoning; Sybil excluded.

entries.title: A Game-theoretic Taxonomy and Survey of Defensive Deception for Cybersecurity and Privacy
entries.attacker_access: Attacker modelled in Nash/Stackelberg games
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can deploy deception (perturbation, MTD, obfuscation, mixing, honey-x, engagement)
entries.setup: Survey of 24 game-theoretic papers (2008-2018)
entries.gaps: Mostly static game models; no agents or merge.

entries.title: A terminology for talking about privacy by data minimization
entries.attacker_access: Attacker observing items of interest relative to an anonymity set
entries.attacker_goal: identify, link or detect subjects/items
entries.gaps: Informal definitions only.

entries.title: The Best-Laid SCHEMEs: Coordinated Sabotage and Monitoring in Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: All agents in the team are instructed saboteurs sharing a plan and communicating under various topologies
entries.attacker_knowledge: Instructed; told or not told about monitor presence
entries.attacker_goal: covert side task needing all agents (sabotage)
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted monitor over code edits, optionally over inter-agent messages; FPR <= 2%
entries.setup: SCHEME: 17 task instances, 7 settings, 8 real open-source libraries; multiple communication topologies; Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT 5.1 Codex
entries.metric: covert+main success; detection rate at FPR<=2%; undetected sabotage
entries.headline: Gemini 3.1 Pro completes covert and legitimate task in 84% of samples (Codex 46%); monitor with messages detects 100% / 81%; undetected sabotage <3%
entries.gaps: All agents corrupted by instruction; no honest majority, no merge into a parent; abstract only.

entries.title: The Distributed Detectability Band Against Marginal-Preserving Attacks
entries.attacker_access: Attacker spreads harm across steps while exactly matching the benign per-step monitor-score marginal
entries.attacker_knowledge: Assumed able to match marginal exactly; adaptive red-teamer on synthetic traces only
entries.attacker_goal: distributed sub-threshold sabotage
entries.defender_assumptions: Marginal monitors (Monitor A) vs sequence monitors (CUSUM, SPRT, HMM, etc.; Monitor B)
entries.setup: Synthetic Gaussian-copula AR(1) traces; real traces from a Qwen2.5-7B agent scored by a Llama-3.2-3B monitor
entries.headline: Marginal monitors at chance (AUC 0.52, KS 0.013); sequence monitors AUC 0.79-0.97; on real traces Monitor B rises from 0.68 to 0.98 with horizon
entries.gaps: Harm modelled as a scalar over steps of one stream, not contributions of parallel parts merged into a parent.

entries.title: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
entries.attacker_access: Agentic coding models with tools (code execution, web search) building stegosystems; agents coordinating without prior agreement
entries.attacker_knowledge: No pre-shared key (Schelling coordination) in the coordination study
entries.attacker_goal: covert channel past monitors
entries.setup: Agentic coding evaluations with tools; Schelling-point coordination metrics (not read beyond abstract)
entries.gaps: Covert channel capability, not merge-time poisoning; abstract only.

entries.title: Trust propagation and structural containment in Multi-agent LLM pipelines
entries.attacker_access: Shared-memory poisoning and indirect prompt injection (forged approval in a retrieved document) at a low-privilege agent; some runs attacker holds signing secret
entries.attacker_goal: propagate compromise to higher-privilege agent and trigger unsafe execution
entries.defender_assumptions: Independent authorisation layer with task-bound signed tokens; separately verified policy oracle; Observer layer
entries.setup: Four-agent LangGraph pipeline (Supervisor, Researcher, Validator, Executor); 60 labelled tasks; 3 seeds; component ablations
entries.metric: Judgment Bypass Rate; Unsafe Action Rate; hijack-detection false positives
entries.headline: Memory poisoning reaches execution in every undefended trial; with authorisation JBR 100% but unsafe actions 0%
entries.gaps: Containment of actions, not repair of corrupted beliefs; single pipeline, small sample.

entries.title: Protecting Mobile Agents Against Malicious Hosts
entries.attacker_access: Host executing the agent can read and modify it, 'brainwash' its memory, replay and probe
entries.attacker_goal: learn secrets; alter agent memory to favour host (integrity)
entries.defender_assumptions: Originator holds decryption; additively homomorphic encryption; non-interactive protocol
entries.setup: Theoretical cryptography; no implementation
entries.headline: Lemma 5/Corollary 6: additively homomorphic encryption on Z/nZ allows CEF for polynomials
entries.gaps: Restricted to polynomials/rational functions; no analogue for natural-language reasoning; DoS and replay remain.

entries.title: SoK: Metadata-Protecting Communication Systems
entries.attacker_access: Global network adversary; anonymity-set manipulation (Sybil add/remove)
entries.attacker_goal: break unlinkability/unobservability
entries.defender_assumptions: Varies by system (non-collusion, honest servers, synchrony)
entries.setup: Systematisation of 31 systems
entries.headline: Only eight of 31 systems reach low latency
entries.gaps: Messaging-centric; no agent workloads or content integrity.

entries.title: Implementing Trustworthy Services Using Replicated State Machines
entries.attacker_access: Compromised replicas fully controlled; mobile adversary moving between servers; shared vulnerabilities across replicas
entries.attacker_goal: compromise more than t replicas; steal service key
entries.defender_assumptions: 2t+1 replicas; independence (questioned); proactive recovery; threshold secret sharing; adversary structures; diversity
entries.headline: With shared vulnerabilities P(more than t compromised) is about Pr1, not Pr1^m (stated, not measured)
entries.gaps: Survey without experiments; deterministic state machine semantics, not semantic LLM outputs.

entries.title: A Survey of Moving Target Defenses for Network Security
entries.attacker_access: Network attacker doing reconnaissance
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can move system elements (Stackelberg commitment)
entries.gaps: Network-centric; no agents or merge.

entries.title: in-toto: Providing farm-to-table guarantees for bits and bytes
entries.attacker_access: Compromise of a supply-chain step (build machine, functionary), with or without key compromise
entries.attacker_goal: ship compromised artifacts
entries.defender_assumptions: Correct signed layout; threshold functionaries fail independently; deterministic artifacts
entries.setup: Retrospective mapping of 30 historical supply-chain compromises onto three deployments (Datadog, Reproducible Builds Debian, cloud-native pipeline)
entries.headline: 23 of 30 historical attacks needed no key compromise and would be caught in all three deployments
entries.gaps: Retrospective, not live attacks; needs deterministic hashable outputs.

entries.title: On Omitting Commits and Committing Omissions: Preventing Git Metadata Tampering
entries.attacker_access: Write access to the Git server, not developer keys; presents inconsistent reference views transiently
entries.attacker_goal: teleport, rollback, delete references to merge untested code or omit patches
entries.defender_assumptions: Signed reference state log in the repo; developers check the log; out-of-band channels exist
entries.setup: Threat analysis, proof-of-concept attacks, defence implementation (evaluation not read in detail)
entries.gaps: Attacks control which authentic contributions are seen, not semantic content; single repository.

entries.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
entries.attacker_access: Lower-privilege text (user messages, tool outputs) carrying conflicting instructions
entries.attacker_goal: prompt injection, jailbreak
entries.defender_assumptions: Model fine-tuned to prioritise system > user > tool content
entries.setup: Synthetic aligned/misaligned instruction data; fine-tuning GPT-3.5
entries.gaps: Per-model filter; offers nothing if a merge imports a part's output at system level or as the parent's own reasoning.

entries.title: State Contamination in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
entries.attacker_access: Toxic or adversarial context seen by an agent that is then compressed into memory summaries
entries.attacker_goal: carry hostile framing into later generations below detector thresholds (memory laundering)
entries.defender_assumptions: Toxicity detectors on summaries; sanitisation before or after summarisation
entries.setup: Paired counterfactual multi-agent rollouts; transcript, summary and memory-buffer channels compared; models not checked
entries.gaps: Toxicity as proxy for adversarial influence; goal-hijack payloads not measured; abstract only.

entries.title: The Predecessor Attack: An Analysis of a Threat to Anonymous Communications Systems
entries.attacker_access: c colluding corrupt members inside the protocol logging predecessors per round
entries.attacker_knowledge: Passive; recognise the session each round
entries.attacker_goal: identify the initiator over repeated path reformations
entries.defender_assumptions: Uniform path selection; helper (fixed first-hop) nodes as defence
entries.setup: Probabilistic analysis plus simulations of static and dynamic membership
entries.headline: Rounds needed roughly O((n/c) log n) for Crowds and O((n/c)^2 ln n) for Onion Routing
entries.gaps: Location leakage over rounds; no content poisoning.

entries.title: System-Level Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks: An Information Flow Control Perspective
entries.attacker_access: Untrusted input reaching the planning process
entries.attacker_goal: compromise plans
entries.defender_assumptions: Security monitor filters untrusted input out of planning; structured executable plans
entries.setup: Formal models, case studies and benchmarks (numbers not read)
entries.gaps: Single-agent planner isolation; implicit flows; abstract only.

entries.title: A Sanctuary for Mobile Agents
entries.attacker_access: One or more malicious servers on the route that can rewrite all mutable agent state; colluding servers can forge itinerary
entries.attacker_goal: brainwash agent (integrity of returned results)
entries.defender_assumptions: Signed code and read-only state; secure channels between honest servers; per-server MAC keys erased before migration (PRACs); secure coprocessor
entries.setup: Analytical argument and protocol design; no implementation results
entries.headline: Two agents on route and its reverse recover the true minimum fare with one malicious server unless it holds the minimum (then second-best)
entries.gaps: Agent replication covers only one malicious server and a minimisation function.
